hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the BTB, the ID-precomputed forwarding and the EX verify logic
(eq_tgt / eq_ft compares of the pc register vs the architectural next PC,
JALR always mispredicts, branch_cond as the last select between redir_c1 and
redir_c0), but register the verdict instead of using it combinationally.

ex_stage:
  * `advance = !stall && !md_stall` (flop-derived: dmem_ready/ex_mem flops and
    muldiv done flop). `redirect_d` = existing redirect expression, with its
    early terms qualified by `advance && !redirect_q` (fold into redir_c1 /
    redir_c0 so the late branch_cond select stays the last mux). A
    redirecting instruction held in EX by a dmem/md stall therefore fires
    only on the cycle it actually advances; pc is held by stall_if
    meanwhile, so the mismatch persists until then.
  * `redirect_q` flop (reset 0) <= redirect_d. The `redirect` output of
    ex_stage becomes `redirect_q`, and `redirect_target` becomes
    `reg_q.pc_next` (EX/MEM.pc_next already holds the redirecting
    instruction's architectural next PC at that cycle; no extra 32 flops;
    it is not overwritten by bubbles, only valid/ctrl are).
  * The instruction in EX during the redirect_q cycle is the wrong-path
    successor and must die: `ex_valid = in.valid && !redirect_q` is used
    for md_op (so it can neither start muldiv nor raise md_stall) and for
    redirect_d. The EX/MEM register takes a bubble (valid=0, ctrl='0, like
    the md_stall bubble) when `redirect_q || md_stall`, with the dmem
    `stall` hold still having top priority.
hazard_unit: `flush_id = redirect_q || (load_use_hazard && !dmem_stall &&
  !md_stall)`. A registered redirect kills in place (id_stage already
  gives flush priority over hold for valid/ctrl, data fields stay
  guarded by !stall), which is required when a false-hit LOAD under
  dmem_stall holds EX/MEM while the wrong-path ID/EX instruction must
  still be killed. The old `redirect &&` suppression by dmem/md stall goes
  away because redirect_q is only set when the redirecting instruction
  advanced and the killed instruction can never be a held MUL/DIV.
if_stage: unchanged pc priority (`redirect` over `!stall`), now with
  `redirect` = redirect_q and target = EX/MEM.pc_next. At the redirect_q
  cycle the pc register still holds the wrong-path B+2 address and is
  rewritten at its end; ID/EX is flushed so nothing from the wrong path
  is captured. The "pc holds the address fetched after the instruction in
  EX" invariant used by eq_tgt/eq_ft still holds after the rewrite.
core.sv: wire redirect/redirect_target as above. BTB training stays on the
EX/MEM register (the killed instruction becomes an EX/MEM bubble so it
cannot train), regfile bypass already covers the branch's write-back, and
rvfi order/pc_wdata are unchanged (pc_next is still actual_next).

Penalty per mispredict goes from 1 to 2 bubbles. Expected: cycles
4.42M -> ~4.55-4.6M (+3-4%), Fmax 79.8 -> ~88-92 MHz if the next paths
(ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result, compare -> pc_next) sit at ~15 ns as the
fanout-free cones suggest. FF/LUT cost ~+2 flops. The registered-redirect
structure also decouples the verify result from pc/stall logic, so
it is the prerequisite for retrying a fetch queue (r4s2/r5s2 lost Fmax to
the stall/redirect cone) without reintroducing that tail.
Verify: cocotb + cosim (all CRCs), formal (liveness, pc_fwd, unique),
and check `make timing` shows the worst path no longer ends at flush_id /
pc; if the next worst path is within ~1 ns of the old one, the hypothesis
is a loss.

title: Single shared branch comparator (one carry chain + MSB fixup) selected by branch_op flops
motivation:
The champion's worst path (18.25 ns, 23 cells) is MEM/WB.ctrl.mem_to_reg
-> wb mux -> EX forward mux (rs1/rs2) -> 32-bit branch compare ->
branch_cond -> redirect -> flush_id -> ID/EX ctrl flops. Prior rounds
re-timed the forward selects (r4s0), the regfile front (r5s1), the redirect
fan-out/endpoint (r2s0, r6s0, r6s1, r6s2) but nobody has touched the
comparator itself. ex_stage.sv writes the branch condition as a 6-way case
of independent operators: rs1==rs2, rs1!=rs2, signed <, signed >=, unsigned
<, unsigned >=. Gowin synthesis builds a separate carry chain per distinct
relational operator (signed and unsigned versions differ in the MSB so they
are not merged), so the post-forward rs1/rs2 nets fan out to ~2-4 chains
plus an XOR/AND equality tree plus the JALR adder plus the EX/MEM operand
flops, and branch_cond then needs a 6:1 mux behind the chains. Both the
fan-out on the forward-mux outputs and the 6:1 select sit directly on the
critical cone.

-> wb mux -> EX forward mux (rs1/rs2) -> 32-bit branch compare ->

re-timed the forward selects (r4s0), the regfile front (r5s1), the redirect
fan-out/endpoint (r2s0, r6s0, r6s1, r6s2) but nobody has touched the

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rewrite only the branch-condition logic in rtl/ex_stage.sv so the
comparator is one 32-bit unsigned `<` chain plus an equality tree, with the
type decoded straight from the ID/EX `ctrl.branch_op` flops (which already
hold funct3: BEQ 000, BNE 001, BLT 100, BGE 101, BLTU 110, BGEU 111, so
op[2]=0 selects eq-type, op[1]=0 selects signed, op[0] inverts):
    eq  = (rs1 == rs2);
    ltu = (rs1 < rs2);                                  // the only chain
    lt  = ltu ^ (!op[1] & (rs1[31] ^ rs2[31]));         // signed fix-up in the
                                                        // MSB only, no wider chain
    branch_cond = (op[2] ? lt : eq) ^ op[0];
The MSB fix-up and the op select are off the carry chain: after the chain
the data signal `ltu` passes through one LUT5-class function
(ltu, x=rs1[31]^rs2[31] (computed in parallel), eq, op[2], op[0] ...)
instead of an operator-specific chain plus a 6:1 case mux. This removes
two to three redundant carry chains (~100 LUT/CLS) and roughly halves the
fan-out of the rs1/rs2 forward-mux output nets, which shortens the routing
hop between the forward mux and the compare and removes one LUT level
behind the chain; branch_taken, misalign_fault and the redir_c1/c0 split are
untouched (branch_cond is still the last select into `redirect`). No pipeline
timing, stall, BTB or RVFI behaviour changes, so cycles stay bit-identical
(~4.42M); the formal branch checks and cosim cover correctness
(BNE/BGE/BGEU = inverted eq/lt/ltu, signed ordering via the MSB xor
identity lt_signed = ltu ^ (a31 ^ b31)). Expected: shave ~0.7-1.2 ns off the

title: Resolve branches in MEM from EX/MEM-registered operands: forward muxes leave the compare->redirect cone
motivation:
A fresh `make timing` on the champion shows all 25 worst setup paths are one
cone: MEM/WB.mem_to_reg flop (fanout 32) -> wb_w_data LUT (fanout 37) -> EX
rs1 forward mux (2 LUT levels) -> 32-bit compare carry chain -> 4 LUT levels
of branch_taken/branch_cond select -> redirect (fanout 63) -> flush_id /
pc mux -> ID/EX RESET pins. Data delay 12.92 ns, of which 7.45 ns is routing:
~4.7 ns is the forward-mux front *before* the carry chain (itself only
~0.7 ns), and ~5 ns is the redirect fan-out tail. Prior attempts only moved
the endpoint (r6s1 registered the verify result, +3.0%; r6s2 -4.5%; r6s0
trimmed flush sinks, -6.7%; r5s0 pre-muxed WB data, ~0) and left the
forward -> compare front in EX. EX/MEM already holds the post-forward
rs1_val/rs2_val flops, so the compare can run in MEM straight from flops and
the ~4.7 ns forward front disappears from the redirect cone. Redirects are
cheap to delay: r6s1 measured +2.3% cycles for one extra bubble on every
EX redirect (~100K redirects per 10 CoreMark iterations).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move branch condition, next-PC verify and the branch-taken misalign trap from
EX into MEM, evaluated from EX/MEM flops; the redirect becomes a MEM-stage
signal with a 2-bubble penalty.
EX keeps only forward mux -> ALU / JALR adder / AGU and registers extra
EX/MEM fields: pred_pc (= fetch_pc, the PC fetched behind this instruction),
br_target (jalr_target for JALR, else in.tgt), pc_plus4, tgt_misal. EX
drops branch_cond, eq_tgt/eq_ft, redir_c0/c1 and the redirect output. The
only fault EX still computes is the jump misalign (JAL: tgt_misal flop; JALR:
jalr_sum[1], a 2-bit cone); that alone feeds misalign_fault_ex into ID's
forward-select precompute, so the old branch_cond -> misalign -> rs?_fwd_*
path (r6s1's worst) is gone (branches never write rd, so the select logic
never needed the branch term).
MEM does what ex_stage.sv does today, from flops: branch_cond from
rs1_val/rs2_val and branch_op, eq_tgt = (pred_pc == br_target) and
eq_ft = (pred_pc == pc_plus4) in parallel, then `redirect = branch_cond ?
redir_c1 : redir_c0` with branch_cond still the last select, actual_next =
jalr_go ? br_target : exp_ft ? pc_plus4 : br_target, branch-taken && tgt_misal
OR-ed into the existing mem_stage ctrl_with_trap, and the architectural
next PC written into MEM/WB.pc_next for RVFI (must stay pc_plus4 on a trap
so pc_fwd holds). A branch in MEM can never coincide with dmem_stall (that
needs a mem op in EX/MEM), so the redirect cannot be dropped by a stall.
When redirect fires from MEM: pc <= actual_next (priority over every stall,
as today), ID/EX is flushed even under md_stall (valid+ctrl clear only), the
instruction currently in EX is prevented from entering EX/MEM (EX/MEM
valid+ctrl clear, so a wrong-path load/store/branch has no effect), and a
MUL/DIV that began in EX behind the branch is cancelled through a new
muldiv `abort` input (FSM back to idle, done=0). This replaces hazard_unit's
`!md_stall` flush suppression, which existed only because redirect came from
EX.
BTB training must not hang off the new late compare: train/invalidate
from the MEM/WB register instead (a one-flop `branch_taken` added to
mem_wb_t; pc = mem_wb.pc, target = mem_wb.pc_next when taken), one cycle
later than today; writes stay idempotent. This keeps btb_train_en (fanout
~430 flop enables) off the compare cone.
Expected effect: the redirect cone shrinks from ~14 LUT levels fed by the
WB-mux/forward front to flop -> compare -> select -> redirect (~9-10 levels,
est. ~10 ns), cutting about 2-3 ns off the dominant cone while the sibling
cones (ALU, load-align, muldiv) sat <= 11.9 ns in r6s1's report; cost is
~+2.5% cycles (second bubble) and ~+100 flops (pred_pc, br_target, pc_plus4,
taken). Net target ~+7%, i.e. Fmax ~88-92 MHz at ~4.53M cycles. Verification

must never retire or write rd), cosim with CoreMark, test_muldiv with abort.

title: Halve EX redirects with a 64-entry 2-bit-hysteresis BTB (+JALR last-target) so a registered (late) redirect pays for itself
motivation:
Offline model on the real CoreMark commit trace (2.94M retired instrs: 532k branches of
which 296k taken, 50k JAL, 13.8k JALR/ret) of the exact current predictor (16-entry
direct-mapped, taken-only, 8-bit tag, trained 3 instrs late, invalidate-on-not-taken)
gives 100.1k EX redirects (branch 73.7k, JAL 12.6k, JALR 13.8k = always). That matches the
cycle log: no-BTB 4.681M -> BTB 4.422M = -259k cycles = (359k - 100k) fewer redirects, i.e.
~1 cycle per redirect. r6s1 (registered/late redirect, 3 bubbles/redirect instead of 2)
then cost +100.9k cycles = exactly 1 per redirect, and gave Fmax 84.07 vs 79.79 but net
only +3.0% (185.88), inside the P&R noise and under the 4.6% bar. So the redirect count is
now the lever that decides whether the Fmax-friendly late redirect nets out: each redirect
removed is worth 1 cycle today and 2 cycles under late redirect. The same model says
capacity/aliasing and the 1-bit taken-only policy are what is left: 64 entries with 2-bit
hysteresis (alloc on taken at 2, +1/-1 saturating, predict when tag matches and ctr>=2)
-> 63.8k redirects; adding JALR last-target prediction (BTB trained with jalr_target)
-> 52.0k; 128 entries only reaches ~45k (not worth 2x the flops). Pure predictor
upgrade on the current EX-redirect core is worth only ~1-2% of cycles (below the 4.6%
bar by itself), which is why it is paired with the late redirect it makes affordable.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
(1) BTB: 64 entries, index pc[7:2], tag pc[13:8] (6 bits; model shows 6 vs 8 tag bits is
identical on CoreMark), target pc[19:2] (18 bits), 2-bit counter per entry replacing the
valid bit (only the counters are reset; ctr==0 means invalid). Lookup stays flop -> 64:1
mux -> 6-bit compare -> next_pc mux (well under 10 ns, no imem_data or EX term).
Training from the EX/MEM register as now: taken branch / JAL / JALR train (alloc at ctr=2 on
tag miss, else saturating +1, target overwritten); not-taken branch decrements only on tag
match. Writes remain idempotent enough under a dmem-stall hold (saturating counters; a
re-train of a held EX/MEM only pushes a counter one extra step, harmless to correctness
because every prediction is verified). For JALR, ex_stage writes
reg_q.branch_target <= is_jalr ? jalr_target : in.tgt (adder -> flop, same depth as the
alu_result endpoint) and the training enable includes is_jalr.
(2) Verification/redirect: stop forcing a redirect on every JALR. EX computes
`mismatch = in.valid && (actual_next[31:2] != fetch_pc[31:2])` for all control types (for
JALR compare jalr_target[31:2], with the misalign-trap path keeping pc+4), but registers it
into a new EX/MEM `redir` flop (+ the corrected next pc already held in reg_q.pc_next) and
applies `pc <= ex_mem.pc_next` plus the ID/EX bubble from the MEM stage (the r6s1
structure: wrong-path instruction in EX is gated by ex_valid = in.valid && !ex_mem.redir
so it cannot redirect, start MUL/DIV, or enter MEM). This ends the forward -> compare ->
redirect -> pc/flush fan-out cone (the 18 ns worst path of the champion) in a single flop,
Fmax 79.8 -> ~84 as measured by r6s1, while the halved redirect count (100k -> ~52k)
absorbs the extra bubble per redirect.
Expected cycles ~ 4.4216M - 48k*1 + 52k*1 ~ 4.43M (flat vs champion) with Fmax ~84, i.e.
~+5% fitness. Cost: ~64*27 = ~1.7k extra flops/~0.6k LUT (budget 10k LUT4 is ample).
If the late-redirect half cannot be made correct, the BTB half alone (items in (1), kept
on the current EX-redirect core) is still a valid, lower-risk (~+1-2%) fallback.

title: 2-entry IF/ID skid queue so backend stalls stop discarding fetched instructions (pc no longer holds), cheap now that the redirect is registered
motivation:
Cycles, not Fmax, are the only lever left that is deterministic. The champion runs 4.4255M cycles
for 2.94M retired instructions (CPI 1.50), while the imem alone (22% stalls, one fetch per cycle)
floors CPI at 1/0.78 = 1.28 (3.77M cycles). The gap (~650k cycles, 15%) exists because stalls add
instead of overlapping: on every backend stall (load-use, dmem stall, MUL/DIV stall) if_stage
freezes pc (stall_if) and the instruction that was just fetched successfully is thrown away and must
win the 22% imem lottery again, and no fetch progress is made while the backend is stalled.
Evidence: r5s2 built exactly a 2-entry fetch queue and measured 4.107M cycles vs 4.4216M (-7.1%,
matching its cycle model: D=1 -5.6%, D=2 -7.2%, D=4 -7.7%), but Fmax fell 66.7 -> 62.4 and the net
was +0.65%. Its worst path (21.8 ns, 41 cells) was regfile -> EX forward -> branch compare ->
*combinational* redirect -> pc / stall fan-out, i.e. the queue's extra loading landed on the EX
compare -> redirect cone. That cone no longer exists in the champion: since r6s1/r7s2 the verify
result is registered into EX/MEM.redir and the redirect (pc, flush_id, queue clear) comes from a
flop, so the verify compare only ends in a fan-out-1 flop. The current worst path (17.3 ns, MEM/WB
read_data -> WB mux -> EX fwd mux -> ALU -> dmem BSRAM address) does not touch fetch at all. So the
Fmax cost that sank r5s2 should mostly be gone, while the ~7% cycle win is independent of Fmax and
of the redirect count (the BTB/late-redirect machinery is unchanged). Lessons r5s2/r4s2 explicitly
say to retry the queue only against a post-regfile design and keep the verify compare off any queue
mux; both conditions now hold.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a 2-entry shift-register skid/fetch queue Q0/Q1 = {pc[31:2], instr} with valid flops qv0/qv1
inside if_stage. pc stays the BTB-directed fetch pointer (imem_addr = pc, BTB lookup,
next_pc = btb_hit ? pred_pc : pc+4, training: ALL UNCHANGED, flop-only) but no longer freezes on
backend stalls. Mirror r5s2's structure (it passed formal/cosim and hit the modelled cycles).

ID view (the combinational IF/ID bundle `out`):
  head_valid = qv0 | imem_ready
  out.pc     = qv0 ? Q0.pc    : pc
  out.pc_plus4 = qv0 ? (Q0.pc + 4) : pc_plus4      (incrementer on Q0.pc flops, off the instr path)
  out.instr  = qv0 ? Q0.instr : (imem_ready ? imem_data : 32'h00000013)
  out.valid  = head_valid
(replaces `flush ? NOP : imem_data` / `!flush`; the `flush` input and hazard_unit.flush_if go away).

Consume / fetch-advance rules (stall_id is exactly today's hazard_unit.stall_id = dmem_stall |
load_use | md_stall; it no longer contains imem_stall and stall_if is deleted):
  consume = !stall_id                           (ID takes the head; id_stage/ID-EX logic unchanged)
  adv     = imem_ready && !(qv1 && stall_id)    (the fetch at pc is accepted: pc <= next_pc)
  store   = adv && (qv0 || stall_id)            (the fetched word is NOT the head being consumed
                                                  this cycle, so it is parked in the queue)
  shift   = consume && qv0                      (Q0 consumed, Q1 moves up)
  base queue = shift ? {Q1} : {Q0,Q1};  then if (store) append {pc, imem_data} in the first free
  slot (qv1 is guaranteed 0 when store && the base queue is non-empty after shift; qv1 && stall_id
  drops the fetch and holds pc, so there is never overflow).

qv1 <= 0 (priority over everything). flush_id = (load_use | redirect) & !dmem_stall & !md_stall is
unchanged: the wrong-path head in ID view during the redirect cycle is bubbled at ID/EX, the
wrong-path instruction in EX is already squashed by ex_valid. Under a dmem stall that holds a
redirecting instruction in MEM the redirect simply clears the queue / rewrites pc every held cycle,
as today.

Verification stays exactly as in the champion and needs NO change in ex_stage/ID-EX: ex_stage's
fetch_pc is if_id_w.pc, which is now `head pc = qv0 ? Q0.pc : pc` -- the address of the instruction

title: Single-source EX forwarding: bypass MEM-stage result into ID/EX, drop MEM/WB->EX leg
motivation:
The champion's worst path (17.28 ns, 12 cells, slack -6.99) runs MEM/WB.read_data ->
wb_stage mem_to_reg mux (u_wb) -> EX forward/operand muxes -> ALU carry chain -> result_sel
-> dmem BSRAM address (EX/MEM.alu_result is absorbed into the BSRAM address register).
The wb_w_data net is a high-fanout, late-arriving source: it also feeds the 31 regfile row
D pins, the regfile write-first bypass, and four EX operand muxes. Lessons so far: endpoint
tweaks (redirect fan-out, hand-shared compare/ALU operators, duplicate AGU) are all inside
the P&R seed spread because the sibling cones are within 1-2 ns; the only steps that moved
Fmax materially cut the *shared front* (regfile BSRAM -> fabric flops, +19%; ID-registered
one-hot forward selects, +4.75%). The MEM/WB -> EX leg is the last late-arriving
shared-front source; r5s0's "pre-mux wb_data" only moved the mux, it did not remove the
leg, and was judged against a different worst path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Remove the MEM/WB -> EX forwarding leg and do the equivalent bypass one stage earlier, in
ID. When instruction I is in ID: I-3 is in WB (already covered by the regfile write-first
bypass), I-1 is in EX (still forwarded in EX next cycle from the EX/MEM.alu_result flop,
unchanged), and I-2 is in MEM. The MEM-stage result of I-2 -- load_data (post align/extend)
when ctrl.mem_to_reg else EX/MEM.alu_result -- is muxed over the regfile read data in ID
(priority: I-2 MEM result over regfile/WB bypass; hit = ex_mem_rd == rs?_addr &&
mem_rw_post_trap && rd != 0 && !rs?_fwd_ex_d, same kill conditions the old rs?_fwd_wb_d
used) and captured into ID/EX.rs?_val together with I. Then EX has a single forward
source: rs1/rs2 = fwd_ex ? EX/MEM.alu_result : rs?_val, and ALU a/b select among REG /
FWD_EX / PCIMM (still one LUT4+MUX2 level, but with no wb mux level and a 35-fanout net
gone from EX). id_ex_t drops rs1_fwd_wb/rs2_fwd_wb and OPSEL_FWD_WB; core.sv no longer
routes wb_w_data into ex_stage; mem_stage exports a combinational mem_result for ID.
Correctness argument for stalls: dmem stall holds ID/EX and EX/MEM together, and a load held
in MEM completes (dmem_ready=1) in exactly the cycle ID/EX can next capture, so the
bypassed value is the delivered load data; load-use still stalls one cycle and the consumer
then sees the load as I-2 (in MEM) with a bubble in EX, exactly as the old fwd_wb timing;
md_stall bubbles EX/MEM so I-2 has retired and been regfile-written before the dependent is
captured. A held instruction in EX no longer depends on the MEM/WB data fields surviving
a stall. Cycle count is unchanged (same stalls, same redirect behaviour), flop count is
slightly lower (two fwd_wb bits). New timing to watch: dmem_rdata (BSRAM DO ~2.3 ns) ->
shift/extend -> mem_to_reg mux -> bypass mux -> ID/EX.rs?_val, estimated ~8-9 ns vs the
~11.4 ns period, and regfile read mux -> bypass -> ID/EX (one extra mux level, flop-to-flop).
Expected: the wb mux level plus its fan-out routing (~1.3-2 ns of the 17.3 ns path) leaves
the shared front, ~+6-8% Fmax at identical cycles; sibling cones (ALU -> EX/MEM,
compare -> redirect) bound the upside. Verify cosim/formal on I-2 load bypass, misaligned
load/store trap kill (mem_rw_post_trap), x0, back-to-back dependent loads under dmem stalls.

EX/MEM.alu_result : rs?_val` source and a 3:1 `a_sel`/`b_sel`) by bypassing the I-2 MEM-stage result (`mem_to_reg ? load_data : alu_result`) over the regfile read in ID and capturing it into ID/EX `rs?_val` scored 205.68 vs the 198.76 champion at unchanged cycles, about half the +6% target and inside the ~6% P&R seed spread, so moving a late bypass one stage earlier mostly relocates the late source instead of removing it (dmem BSRAM DO -> align/extend -> mem_to_reg -> bypass mux -> ID/EX now carries what the `wb_w_data` mux carried in EX, and the regfile read mux gains a level), while the sibling ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result and compare -> redirect cones sit only ~1-2 ns behind; no post-change worst-path report was recorded so this is inferred, but with r4s0 (+4.75%) it says the forward-mux front is worth ~+3-5% per cut and is nearly spent, so take the next target from a fresh worst-path report (and check the new load-data -> ID/EX path in it) rather than another forward-source restructure.

title: Zero-extra-bubble late redirect: bypass the registered MEM redirect target onto the fetch address (1 wasted slot per mispredict instead of 2)
motivation:
The champion (198.76, 4.4255M cycles, 87.96 MHz) resolves every BTB mispredict in EX but
only registers it (EX/MEM.redir / pc_next) and applies it from MEM with `pc <= pc_next`.
The corrected target is therefore fetched one cycle after the redirect flop is set, which
is why r6s1's late redirect cost exactly +1 cycle per redirect (+100.9k cycles over
~100k redirects) relative to the old EX redirect. r7s2 then halved the redirect count
(100k -> ~52k) to pay for that cycle. The cycle is not inherent: `redir` and `pc_next` are
flops, so the fetch address can be `redirect ? pc_next : pc` in the SAME cycle the redirect
flop is set (a 2:1 mux on flop outputs in front of the pc/BTB-lookup/pc+4 logic), which
fetches the correct-path instruction one cycle earlier. The remaining wrong-path slot is
only the instruction already in EX behind the redirecting one, which ex_stage already
squashes via ex_valid = in.valid && !reg_q.redir. That puts the late redirect at the same
1-bubble penalty the old EX redirect had, with the Fmax-friendly registered verify kept.
Predictor headroom check (honest): ~52k redirects x 2 bubbles = ~104k cycles = ~2.3% of
the 4.4255M cycles; a perfect predictor could save at most that, so further BTB
capacity/history work (128 entries -> ~45k redirects) is worth <0.4% and is not worth
its flops. Cutting the per-redirect penalty is the only predictor-side lever left that is
worth ~1.2% of cycles (52k saved), and it costs essentially no Fmax because in the timed
netlist imem_data is an LFSR flop that does not depend on imem_addr (fpga/core_bench_si.sv),
so a mux in front of imem_addr is not on any imem_addr -> imem_data -> decode path; the only
new paths are flop -> mux -> (BTB lookup | pc+4 | pc+imm adder) -> flop, all well under the
~17 ns worst path (WB -> fwd mux -> ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
(1) if_stage: form `fpc = redirect ? redirect_target : pc`. Drive imem_addr, out.pc, the
BTB lookup index/tag (fpc[7:2], fpc[13:8]), pc_plus4 = fpc + 4, pred_pc high bits
{fpc[31:20], tgt, 2'b00} and next_pc from fpc. pc update becomes
`if (reset) pc <= RESET_PC; else if (!stall) pc <= next_pc; else pc <= fpc;`
(stalled with redirect still writes the target into pc so it is not lost; stalled without
redirect fpc == pc so pc just holds). The old `redirect` priority arm is gone because it is
folded into fpc. out.pc = fpc keeps ex_stage's fetch_pc invariant ("address of the
instruction in ID = address fetched after the instruction in EX"): while redirect is set
the instruction in EX is squashed and its verify is gated by ex_valid, and otherwise
fpc == pc exactly as today. No change to ex_stage's redir/pc_next generation is needed
(only a comment).
(2) hazard_unit: the correct-path instruction now sits in ID during the redirect cycle, so
`redirect` must NOT flush it: flush_id = load_use_hazard_eff && !dmem_stall && !md_stall
with load_use_hazard_eff = load_use_hazard && !redirect. The load-use compare reads
ID/EX (the squashed wrong-path instruction in EX), so it must be masked by redirect or a
wrong-path load would stall/bubble the correct-path target. stall_if / stall_id use the
masked hazard as well (md_stall is already 0 under redirect because md_op uses ex_valid).
(3) id_stage: its forward precompute looks at ID/EX (the "I-1" slot) which, during the
redirect cycle, holds the squashed wrong-path instruction, not the architectural
predecessor of the target now in ID (that is the redirecting instruction B, currently in
EX/MEM and next cycle in MEM/WB). Add a `squash_idex` input (= redirect) and use
idex_wr = ctrl.reg_write && rd != 0 && !squash_idex, so rs?_fwd_ex is never set from the
wrong-path slot and rs?_fwd_wb (from ex_mem_rd/ex_mem_rw = B) still picks up B's result.
Without this mask the target's operands would be forwarded from a bubble in EX/MEM.
(4) core.sv: wire redirect into hazard_unit (already there) and a new squash_idex into
id_stage; no port-shape change on `core`.
Correctness notes the implementer must keep: dmem stall with redirect asserted (a falsely
predicted load/store held in MEM) keeps EX/MEM and redir frozen, ID/EX holds, pc <= fpc
(target) every held cycle, and the target is captured into ID/EX on the release cycle
(redir still set that cycle, ex_stage clears it as before); imem stall with redirect
produces a NOP bubble into ID/EX (flush_if) and pc <= target; the BTB train/decrement
path from EX/MEM is untouched; RVFI order/valid are unaffected because wrong-path slots
have valid=0. Expected effect: ~52k fewer cycles (4.4255M -> ~4.373M, ~+1.2% iter/cycle),
Fmax flat (flop -> 2:1 mux -> BTB lookup is ~8-10 ns; flush_id loses its redirect term).
Fallback if the BTB lookup after the mux turns out to be timing-critical: keep the lookup
on `pc` only and, in a redirect cycle, predict fall-through (next_pc = fpc + 4); this
forfeits only back-to-back taken-branch targets (rare) and keeps the 1-bubble penalty.
Risk: this is a ~1-2% change, below the 4.6% acceptance bar on its own; it is proposed
because the redirect-count lever is nearly spent (perfect prediction is worth <=2.3%) and
this is the one predictor-side change with a verifiable, deterministic cycle saving.

title: Trim both ends of the forward->ALU->dmem-address cone: pre-muxed split WB flops and no result_sel level
motivation:
The champion's worst path (r7s2, 12 cells) is MEM/WB.read_data flop -> cpu/u_wb (the
`mem_to_reg ? read_data : alu_result` LUT) -> EX forward mux -> ALU -> a final u_ex LUT
(result_sel) -> dmem BSRAM address pin (Gowin absorbs the EX/MEM.alu_result flop into the
BSRAM address register, so the ALU result tail feeds the macro directly). In the last
ten worst-path records, `cpu/u_mem/reg_q.ctrl.mem_to_reg` is the startpoint seven times
(r5s1, r6s0, r6s1, r6s2, r7s0, r7s1, r8s2): it is a fan-out-32 select into the WB mux,
and the WB mux output (`wb_w_data`) then fans out to 31 regfile rows, the two regfile
write-first bypass muxes and four EX forward muxes. The lessons show that the redirect

Two edits, both pure restructuring with identical cycle counts (cycles stay 4,425,510):

(1) Head: pre-mux the WB data in MEM and split it by consumer. mem_stage computes

title: Forward at the operand register: capture the EX ALU result straight into ID/EX a_val/b_val so EX has no forward muxes
motivation:
The champion's worst path (17.28 ns, 12 cells, slack -6.99) is MEM/WB.read_data -> wb_stage
mem_to_reg mux (u_wb) -> EX forward / a_sel operand muxes -> ALU carry chain / op mux ->
result_sel -> dmem BSRAM address. Every EX cone (ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result/BSRAM address,
rs1/rs2 -> compare -> redir, rs1+imm -> eq_jalr -> redir) starts with the same front:
a high-fan-out wb mux plus a 3-source forward mux plus the a_sel/b_sel mux, in front of the
adder. Prior rounds cut that front piecemeal: r4s0 registered the selects (+4.75%), r8s1
moved only the I-2 (MEM/WB) leg into ID (+3.48%, below the 4.6% bar), r7s1 moved branch
resolve to MEM (+5.67%). None removed the I-1 (EX/MEM.alu_result -> EX) leg, and the front
stays on the critical path because a late-arriving forwarded value always has to go through
mux levels *before* the adder. The classic alternative is to put the bypass mux *after* the
ALU, in front of the operand register of the next instruction ("result-to-operand-register
bypass"): the late ALU result then passes through exactly one 2:1 LUT level on its way to the
ID/EX flop, and every EX consumer (ALU, compare, JALR adder, store data, MUL/DIV) reads plain
flops. The select inputs of that final mux (register-number compares against ID/EX.rd and
EX/MEM.rd, decode of AUIPC / alu_src) come from IF/ID flops and are early, so only the data
input is on the critical path. Cycle count is unchanged (same stalls, same redirects), and
the extra cost is ~64 flops plus ~3x32 LUT-level muxes (5225 LUT4 of a 10000 budget).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the operand path so EX contains no forwarding and no operand-select muxes:

(1) id_ex_t: replace rs1_fwd_ex/rs1_fwd_wb/rs2_fwd_ex/rs2_fwd_wb/a_sel/b_sel with two final
ALU-operand flops a_val and b_val (a_val = AUIPC ? pc : forwarded rs1; b_val = alu_src ? imm
: forwarded rs2). Keep rs1_val / rs2_val as the *forwarded* register values (rs2_val is the
store write data and the RVFI rs2_rdata; rs1_val is RVFI-only and pruned in the timed
netlist). Drop OPSEL_* from core_pkg.sv.

(2) id_stage.sv: form the final operand at ID/EX capture time, youngest producer wins:
    rs?_fwd = idex_hit_rs? ? ex_result            // I-1 in EX: result_sel (late data)
            : exmem_hit_rs? ? mem_result          // I-2 in MEM: mem_to_reg ? load_data : EX/MEM.alu_result
            : rf_rs?_data;                        // I-3 and older: regfile (write-first WB bypass kept)
with idex_hit = ID/EX.ctrl.reg_write && ID/EX.rd != 0 && ID/EX.rd == rs? && !jump_misal_ex,
exmem_hit = mem_rw_post_trap && EX/MEM.rd != 0 && EX/MEM.rd == rs?. jump_misal_ex is the
early part of the old misalign_fault (is_jump && (is_jalr ? jalr_sum[1] : tgt_misal)); branches
never write rd so the branch_taken term of misalign_fault is not needed for gating and the late
compare stays out of the select. a_val additionally takes pc for AUIPC (select gated so the
I-1 hit never overrides pc) and b_val takes imm when alu_src (same gating). The hit terms are
pure functions of IF/ID instruction bits and ID/EX / EX/MEM flops, so only ex_result is a late
data input and it sees one LUT level before the flop. All captures remain under the existing
!stall_id enable; the dmem / md stall hold the whole pipe, so a held ID/EX already contains the
final operands and nothing goes stale (this also removes the old need for muldiv to latch
operands against moving forward sources, though that latch can stay as is).

(3) ex_stage.sv: delete the fwd_ex_mem / fwd_mem_wb inputs and the rs1/rs2/alu_a/alu_b muxes.
ALU a/b = in.a_val / in.b_val; branch compare uses a_val/b_val (branches have alu_src=0, so
a_val = rs1 and b_val = rs2); jalr_sum = a_val + b_val (JALR has alu_src=1, b_val = imm);
store write_data = in.rs2_val; muldiv a/b = a_val/b_val (R-type); RVFI rs1/rs2 values come
from in.rs1_val / in.rs2_val. Export ex_result (= result_sel, the value written to
EX/MEM.alu_result: ALU / pc+4 for jumps / muldiv result) and jump_misal_ex to ID. Everything
else (late registered redir, BTB verify against fetch_pc, bubble handling) is unchanged and its
cones now start directly at flops.

(4) mem_stage.sv: export mem_result = mem_to_reg ? load_data : in.alu_result (combinational,
for the ID bypass). hold_wb/data retention in MEM/WB is no longer needed for EX forwarding but
can stay (harmless). core.sv: drop the fwd_mem_wb / fwd_ex_mem wiring into ex_stage, route
ex_result, jump_misal_ex and mem_result into id_stage; wb_w_data now feeds only the regfile and
RVFI, removing the ~40-fan-out wb net from every EX cone.

Correctness notes for the implementer: (a) load-use stays exactly as is (one bubble), so the
load result is never needed from EX; after the bubble the load is I-2 and is bypassed from
mem_result. (b) A bubble / squashed EX instruction has ctrl=0 so idex_hit is 0. (c) MUL/DIV in
EX never lets the consumer capture while md_stall (stall_id), and the cycle md_done is raised
the consumer captures md_result through ex_result. (d) A dmem-stalled load completes in the
cycle ID/EX can next capture, so mem_result carries the delivered data. (e) Verify with the
cocotb suites, cosim (back-to-back dependent ALU ops, load -> bubble -> use, jal/jalr link
forwarding incl. misaligned-target trap kill, misaligned load trap kill via mem_rw_post_trap,
x0, store-data forwarding, MUL -> dependent op) and riscv-formal (the formal wrapper checks
rvfi rs1/rs2 rdata, so keep rs?_val = the forwarded register values).

Expected timing: the wb mux (high fan-out) and the 3:1 forward + 4:1 operand mux levels leave
the front of every EX cone; the new endpoint (ALU -> result_sel -> 1 LUT -> ID/EX flop) is
about one LUT level longer than the old ALU -> EX/MEM end, but the old front was ~2-3 LUT
levels plus the heavily loaded wb_w_data route, so net ~1-2 LUT levels (~1.5-3 ns of the
~11.4 ns period) leave the worst cones at unchanged cycle count. The ID-stage flop-to-flop
paths (regfile 32:1 read -> bypass -> final fwd mux -> ID/EX) gain one LUT level but stay well
under the period. Sibling cones (compare -> redir, BSRAM DO -> align -> MEM/WB) sit 1-2 ns
behind, so the realised gain is bounded at roughly +8%.

title: Decouple branch direction from the BTB: gshare-indexed 2-bit PHT with a history snapshot carried down the pipe, BTB keeps targets only
motivation:
The champion (198.76, Fmax 87.96 MHz, 4.4255M cycles for 2.94M retired
instructions) pays 2 bubbles per EX-detected fetch mismatch (registered
EX/MEM.redir, applied from MEM). r7s2's offline CoreMark replay puts the
remaining redirects at ~52k (about 104k cycles, 2.35% of all cycles), of
which ~45k are conditional-branch mispredicts (~8.5% of the 532k dynamic
branches), ~2k JALR last-target misses and a few thousand JAL / aliasing
misses. The direction state is a 2-bit counter living INSIDE the BTB entry,
so it has three weaknesses: (a) it is bimodal, with no correlation with
earlier branches (CoreMark's list-find / state-machine / crc branches are
history-correlated, and loop exits are periodic); (b) a not-taken branch
decays the counter to 0, which also invalidates the TARGET, so a branch
that alternates pays a full BTB miss plus re-allocation instead of just a
direction flip; (c) any taken branch that aliases onto a hot set evicts
it immediately (alloc at ctr=2 on tag miss).
Honest sizing: the predictor ceiling here is small. Even removing every
redirect is worth ~2.4% of cycles, and the sibling results (16->64 entries,
64->128 entries ~ -7k redirects) say capacity alone is ~0.3%. This is
therefore a low-risk, flop-only change aimed at the largest remaining
predictor term (conditional-branch direction), expected to recover roughly
a quarter to a third of the 45k branch mispredicts (~25-30k cycles, ~0.6%
of cycles) plus ~0.3% from smarter replacement. It will not clear the 4.6%
acceptance bar by itself unless P&R noise helps; the lessons (r2s2, r3s2,
r7s2, r8s2) show that anything touching the fetch cone must stay off
imem_data and off the redirect flop, so this design only adds flop->flop
logic in if_stage and a few payload bits.

it immediately (alloc at ctr=2 on tag miss).
Honest sizing: the predictor ceiling here is small. Even removing every
redirect is worth ~2.4% of cycles, and the sibling results (16->64 entries,
64->128 entries ~ -7k redirects) say capacity alone is ~0.3%. This is
therefore a low-risk, flop-only change aimed at the largest remaining
predictor term (conditional-branch direction), expected to recover roughly
a quarter to a third of the 45k branch mispredicts (~25-30k cycles, ~0.6%
of cycles) plus ~0.3% from smarter replacement. It will not clear the 4.6%
acceptance bar by itself unless P&R noise helps; the lessons (r2s2, r3s2,
r7s2, r8s2) show that anything touching the fetch cone must stay off
imem_data and off the redirect flop, so this design only adds flop->flop
logic in if_stage and a few payload bits.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
(1) Split the BTB entry into {tag[5:0], target[17:0], uncond, valid-ish}
(target store, replaced only on tag conflict) and a separate 64x2-bit
pattern history table (PHT) indexed gshare-style by pc[7:2] ^ ghr[5:0].
Prediction (flops only: pc, ghr -> index -> 64:1 muxes): taken iff
BTB tag matches && (uncond || PHT[idx][1]). JAL / JALR set `uncond`
(always taken, target = last target) so they never depend on the PHT;
conditional branches use the PHT. Lookup depth is the same 64:1 mux +
6-bit compare as today (the PHT read is parallel to the tag compare), so
the fetch cone is unchanged and still independent of imem_data and of the
redirect flop.
(2) History / snapshot: ghr[5:0] is a non-speculative global history of
RESOLVED conditional-branch outcomes (shifted from the EX/MEM register in
the same place BTB training happens, no repair logic needed). To train
the PHT entry that actually made the prediction, the fetch-time
PHT index (6 bits) is carried IF -> ID/EX -> EX/MEM as a payload field
(+12 flops, flop-to-flop only; if_id_t / id_ex_t / ex_mem_t gain `pht_idx`).
Training from EX/MEM (one cycle per instruction, as today): conditional
branch -> PHT[snap_idx] saturating +1 if taken, -1 if not; shift ghr.
Because ghr lags the fetch point by the 2-3 in-flight branches, the index
is slightly stale, but the staleness is consistent between predict and
train (the snapshot is the exact index used), so it only dilutes the
correlation gain, never correctness.
(3) BTB replacement hysteresis: on a taken branch / jump whose tag misses
an occupied entry, do not overwrite on the first conflict: a 1-bit
`conf` on the entry is cleared first (stays valid, target kept) and the
entry is replaced only on a second consecutive conflict; a tag hit sets
conf. This protects hot loop-back branches from one-shot cold taken
branches in the same set (the 64-entry model leaves ~7k redirects of
aliasing on the table: 52k -> 45k at 128 entries).
(4) Every prediction remains verified in EX exactly as today (fetch_pc vs
architectural next PC -> registered EX/MEM.redir, MEM applies it), so
aliasing / stale history / wrong PHT index can only cost cycles. ex_stage,
hazard_unit and the late-redirect structure are untouched except for
forwarding the snapshot index. Not-taken-predicted branches never
redirect; a taken branch with a BTB miss or ctr<2 still pays the same 2
bubbles as now, so the worst case equals the champion.
Cost: PHT 64x2 + conf 64 + uncond 64 flops + 12 pipe flops (~270 FF,
~150 LUT4); budgets are ample. Expected: ~-25k..-35k cycles (-0.6..-0.8%),
Fmax flat; result most likely inside the P&R noise. If the cosim cycle
count shows < -15k cycles, the change should be dropped rather than
tuned, per r8s2's lesson that sub-2% cycle changes cannot be validated.

title: Raw-word-only MEM->ID load bypass: sub-word loads at distance 2 take a load-use bubble instead of the BSRAM->align->bypass cone
motivation:
The champion's worst path (r9s1 log: arrival 15.26 ns, slack -4.97, 8 logic cells) is
dmem BSRAM DO (dmem_2_dmem_2_0_0_s) -> cpu/u_mem load align / sign-extend ->
cpu/u_id 3:1 operand bypass mux -> ID/EX reg_q.rs2_val_16 (a sign-extension-region bit).
That cone is long for three reasons: (a) the BSRAM DO launches late (~2.3+ ns clk->DO),
(b) mem_stage builds load_data with a 4:1 byte-lane mux, a sign-bit select and a
width/sext case, so the sign bit (and its fan-out to bits 31:8) is 3-4 LUT levels deep, and
(c) the aligned value is then fanned out to four ID/EX operand flops per bit (rs1_val,
rs2_val, a_val, b_val) plus MEM/WB.read_data, so the sign bit drives ~100 sinks, with a
3:1 bypass mux in front of every one. Prior cuts of the forward front (r4s0, r8s1, r9s0)
netted ~0-5% because they relocated the late source; r9s1 finally removed the EX-side front.
The load-data -> ID/EX leg is the one the r9s1 lesson flagged as the likely next bound, and
it has not been touched. The key observation is that the full-alignment bypass is only
*needed* for a very narrow case: a LB/LBU/LH/LHU whose consumer is exactly two
instructions behind (distance 2) and is not already held by a load-use bubble.
Word loads (LW, the dominant load in CoreMark's pointer-chasing / matrix / list code)
need no alignment at all, and distance-1 consumers already take the existing load-use
bubble, which also moves the preceding load into WB where the regfile's write-first
bypass serves it from flops (e.g. `lh a;lh b;mul a,b` already stalls on b and so
gets a for free).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Bypass only the RAW word `dmem_rdata` from MEM into the ID/EX operand registers (valid for
LW, where load_data == dmem_rdata when aligned), and make a distance-2 consumer of a
sub-word load wait one cycle with the existing load-use bubble mechanism, picking the value
up from the regfile write-first path (MEM/WB flops) when the load is in WB.
This shortens the worst cone from BSRAM DO -> (byte mux, sign mux, width/sext case) ->
3:1 bypass mux -> 4 operand flops to BSRAM DO -> 3:1 bypass mux -> flop (the align/sign
logic remains only on the BSRAM DO -> MEM/WB.read_data endpoint, which has one flop sink per
bit instead of four and no bypass mux), and removes the high-fan-out sign-extension net from
the ID bypass entirely.

Changes:
(1) mem_stage.sv: `load_data_o` becomes the raw `dmem_rdata` (rename to `load_word_o`);
    MEM/WB.read_data keeps capturing the fully aligned/extended `load_data` unchanged.
(2) id_stage.sv: input `mem_is_load` becomes `mem_is_lw` = EX/MEM.ctrl.mem_to_reg &&
    EX/MEM.ctrl.mem_width == 2 (flop-derived). The sel_ld term is
    `hitX_mem && mem_is_lw && !hitX_ex`. For a misaligned LW the existing
    mem_rw_post_trap gating already kills hit_mem. For a sub-word load in MEM with a
    matching consumer in ID, `rsX_early` would pick `mem_alu` (the address, wrong data),
    but no extra mux term is needed: the new hazard term below is a superset of that
    condition (same EX/MEM flops, same rd compare, ignores the trap qualifier), so
    stall_id is asserted in that cycle and the ID/EX data fields are HELD (not captured)
    while flush_id bubbles valid/ctrl. The consumer is re-captured the next cycle, when the
    load is in WB and the regfile write-first bypass returns the correct value.
    Add a comment documenting that invariant.
(3) hazard_unit.sv: extend `load_use_hazard` with a second term for the load in MEM:
    `ex_mem_sub_ld && ex_mem_rd != 0 && (ex_mem_rd == if_id_rs1 || ex_mem_rd == if_id_rs2)`
    where `ex_mem_sub_ld = EX/MEM.ctrl.mem_to_reg && EX/MEM.ctrl.mem_width != 2`
    (pure EX/MEM flops; ignore the misalign trap -- an unneeded 1-cycle bubble on a
    trapping halfword load is harmless). It is stalled/bubbled exactly like the existing
    load-use (stall_if/stall_id/flush_id): the PC holds, ID/EX gets a bubble, and the
    next cycle the sub-word load is in WB (EX/MEM now holds the bubble) so no further stall
    occurs and no livelock is possible. Existing dmem_stall / md_stall precedence
    (`flush_id = (load_use || redirect) && !dmem_stall && !md_stall`) is unchanged;
    the new term can overlap md_stall, which only holds the bubble off one more cycle and
    is safe because EX/MEM already carries a bubble during md stalls.
(4) core.sv: wire the raw word into id_stage (`mem_load`), `mem_is_lw` from
    ex_mem_w.ctrl, and the new hazard_unit inputs (EX/MEM mem_to_reg, mem_width, rd).

Cost: ~one extra 5-bit equality pair and a 4-input OR level on the stall path (shared
compares with the existing hit1_mem/hit2_mem terms); cycles: +1 only for a sub-word load
followed at distance 2 by a consumer (est. <=0.5-1% of the 4.4255M cycles); zero new flops.
RVFI/formal: the bubble only inserts a cycle, retirement order and values are unchanged
(the consumer reads the regfile value written by the retiring load via the write-first
bypass). The load-use path is already exercised by riscv-formal liveness/bypass checks.
Fitness math: at a ~10.5 ns period the champion needs >=~99.1 MHz (period <=10.09 ns) to
clear the 4.6% bar, i.e. ~0.5 ns off the critical cone; removing 2-3 LUT/MUX levels and a
~100-sink sign-bit net from the worst path is worth ~1-2 ns on that cone, so the sibling
cones (ex_result -> ID/EX, ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result, imem_data -> stall CE) set the new
ceiling, which is why the estimate is moderate.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-001-r10s0 (improvement, +5.50%): Bypassing only the raw `dmem_rdata` word (LW) from MEM into the ID/EX operand flops and making a distance-2 consumer of a LB/LBU/LH/LHU take one extra `load_use_hazard` bubble (new `ex_mem_sub_ld` term from EX/MEM flops, consumer then reads the load from the regfile write-first path in WB) scored 225.90 vs the 214.12 champion, just under the +6% estimate and inside the ~6% P&R seed spread, so it is a small but positive win from taking the BSRAM DO -> byte-lane/sign-extend -> 3:1 bypass -> four operand flops (~100-sink sign bit) cone, which r8s1/r9s1 flagged as the next bound, off the bypass at a modeled cost of <=1% cycles (sub-word load with a consumer exactly 2 behind); no worst-path report or cycles/Fmax split was recorded, so the Fmax-vs-cycles attribution is inferred, but the pattern is to trade a rare, cheap bubble for removing alignment/sign logic from a late bypass, and the correctness invariant is that the hazard term must be a superset of every case where the narrowed bypass picks the wrong source (here `mem_alu` for a sub-word load), using the same EX/MEM flops and rd compare while ignoring the trap qualifier, so ID/EX is held and bubbled rather than capturing the wrong value.

title: Flatten the BSRAM load-data bypass into one early-one-hot AND-OR feeding the ID/EX operand flops
motivation:
The champion (214.12, median Fmax 94.758 MHz, seeds 100.3 / 94.8 / 94.8) is bound by
exactly one family of paths. The recorded worst path (log.jsonl r9s1, slack -4.967 ns at
the 5 ns scoring constraint, 8 cells) runs from the dmem BSRAM (dmem_2_dmem_2_0_0_s, DO
clk->out ~2.3 ns) through cpu/u_mem (load byte/half align + sign/zero extend) into cpu/u_id
(3:1 bypass mux ex_result / mem_load / early value, plus the AUIPC / alu_src operand
select) and ends at the ID/EX rs?_val / a_val / b_val flops. Everything on that path
except the BSRAM is serial LUT levels that were written as a priority chain of muxes:
(a) 4:1 byte-lane select by addr[1:0] and a width select (word / half / byte),
(b) a sign-extend select whose sign bit is itself a late 4:1 mux of DO bits,
(c) sel_ld ? mem_load : early, then sel_ex ? ex_result : ..., then the alu_src / auipc
fold. Every select signal on that path (mem_width, mem_sext, alu_result[1:0], the hit
terms) is an EARLY function of flops, only the 32 DO bits (and ex_result) are late, yet
the synthesis netlist treats the whole chain as data-dependent depth (~4-5 LUT levels
after the 2.3 ns BSRAM). Prior rounds (r3s0, r4s0, r8s1, r9s0) trimmed levels on the EX
forward front piecemeal and mostly relocated the late source; the r9s1 operand-register
bypass was the first cut to clear the seed spread because it removed a whole front at
once. The next whole-front cut is the BSRAM-launched cone that r9s1 itself exposed as
the new worst path. A load-use stall to avoid the path altogether (drop the MEM-stage
load bypass) would cost ~+1 bubble on every dist-1 / dist-2 load consumer (est. 5-8% of
cycles), which is more than the gain, so keep zero extra cycles and instead restructure
the logic.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rewrite the I-2 load bypass so that, for every ID/EX operand bit, the late BSRAM data
passes through ONE AND-OR level (two LUT4 levels at most) with all selects pre-decoded
from flops, instead of align -> sext -> width -> sel_ld -> sel_ex -> alu_src muxes.

(1) mem_stage.sv: stop exporting the aligned `load_data_o` to ID. Export the raw word
`ld_raw = dmem_rdata` plus a small set of EARLY one-hot lane-select signals computed only
from EX/MEM flops (ctrl.mem_width, ctrl.mem_sext, alu_result[1:0], ctrl.mem_to_reg):
  - low byte, bits [7:0]  : l0 (take DO[i]), l1 (DO[8+i]), l2 (DO[16+i]), l3 (DO[24+i])
    where l0 = word | half&!a1 | byte&a==0, l1 = byte&a==1, l2 = half&a1 | byte&a==2,
    l3 = byte&a==3 (word/half/byte x address decode folded into one-hot).
  - bits [15:8]           : m_same (DO[i], word | half&!a1), m_hi (DO[i+16], half&a1),
    plus the sign-fill selects below.
  - bits [31:16]          : w_hi (DO[i], word only) plus the sign-fill selects.
  - sign fill (sext only) : s7 = byte&a==0, s15 = byte&a==1 | half&!a1, s23 = byte&a==2,
    s31 = byte&a==3 | half&a1, each ANDed with mem_sext. Sign-fill terms are ANDed into
    each upper bit separately (DO[7]&s7 | DO[15]&s15 | DO[23]&s23 | DO[31]&s31), i.e. the
    sign bit is NOT first reduced to a shared high-fan-out net, so the whole load extract
    is a flat 4-6 term AND-OR over raw DO bits with early one-hot selects. The existing
    aligned `load_data` stays for MEM/WB.read_data (its path ends at a flop and is not
    critical).
(2) id_stage.sv: build each of rs1_fwd / rs2_fwd / a_d / b_d as a single flat OR of
AND terms:
  d = sel_ex & ex_result | sel_early & early_value | OR_k (sel_ld & lane_sel_k & DO_k)
with sel_ex / sel_ld / sel_early mutually exclusive and one-hot, computed per operand
from IF/ID instruction bits, ID/EX / EX/MEM flops and the jump_misal_ex / mem_rw_post_trap
gating that r9s1 already uses (so trap-killed reg_write is still never forwarded; the
hit_ex-over-hit_mem priority and the AUIPC / alu_src gating are folded into the selects,
not into data muxes). Only ex_result and the 32 raw DO bits remain late data inputs;
everything else is early. Functionally identical to the champion, so cycles are
unchanged (4,425,510).
(3) core.sv: wire the raw word and the lane-select bundle from mem_stage to id_stage
(replace the mem_load port). No change to hazard_unit, ex_stage, BTB or the redirect
path.

Expected effect: the BSRAM -> ID/EX cone drops from ~5 LUT levels to ~2 behind the BSRAM
DO, i.e. roughly 2-3 ns off the worst path at zero cycle cost, for a few hundred LUT4 of
extra select / duplicated AND terms (budget is 5219 of 10000 LUT4). The ex_result -> ID/EX
path is also a flat AND-OR term now (one level, as before). Risk: sibling cones
(ALU/shifter -> result_sel -> EX/MEM / ID/EX, compare -> redir) sit 1-2 ns behind per the
lessons, so the realised gain may be capped there; the median of three P&R seeds must
reach ~99 MHz for the 4.6% bar. Verify with cosim and formal (the load bypass for LB/LBU/
LH/LHU at all four byte offsets, sext and zext, with a back-to-back consumer at distance 2,
and the dmem-stall release cycle).

Replace the mem_load priority-mux chain with a flat per-bit AND-OR: sel_ex & ex_result | sel_early & early | sel_ld & (lane-select terms over raw DO bits incl. sign fill), with mutually-exclusive selects pre-decoded per operand (rs1_fwd, rs2_fwd, a_d, b_d) and AUIPC / alu_src / jump_misal_ex / mem_rw_post_trap gating folded into the selects.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-002-r10s1 (regression, +2.86%): Keeping every load-bypass case and rewriting the BSRAM DO -> byte-lane/sign-extend -> `sel_ld`/`sel_ex`/alu_src chain as one flat AND-OR over the raw `dmem_rdata` word with 13 early one-hot lane/sign-fill selects (`ld_extract` per operand, selects ANDed with `sel_ld`, mem_stage exporting the raw word instead of `load_data`) scored 220.24 vs the 214.12 champion at unchanged cycles, about half the +5% estimate and inside the ~6% P&R seed spread, and below same-round r10s0 (225.90, +5.50%), which deleted the sub-word align/extend from the bypass outright for a rare extra bubble; no worst-path report or cycles/Fmax split was recorded so the cause is inferred, but "one AND-OR level" is not two LUT4 levels on Gowin (each upper bit ORs 5 sign/lane products plus the `ex_result` and early legs, so >=3 levels, and each raw DO sign bit still drives ~100 sinks across the four operands), meaning that against a BSRAM-launched cone, deleting logic from the late path (r10s0) beats re-expressing it with early selects, so prefer removing a late-path case for a cheap bubble over flattening it, and only flatten a mux whose product count fits one LUT4 level (<=2 products per output bit).

title: Depth-1 fetch skid register: bank the fetched head instruction during ID stalls so imem failures are hidden
motivation:
Pure predictor work is capped: the champion has ~52k EX redirects x 2 bubbles = ~104k of
4.4255M cycles (2.35%) even if every one were removed, which is below the 4.6% acceptance bar
(r3s2/r7s2 banked the cheap capacity/hysteresis/JALR wins; r9s2's gshare lost on Fmax). The
front-end loss that IS large is fetch-side: 2.94M retired instrs need 2.94M successful fetches,
and with ~22% imem failures that is ~3.77M of the 4.43M cycles. Every ID-stage stall (load-use,
dmem stall, MUL/DIV stall) currently holds `pc` and throws away the instruction that imem
delivered this cycle (IF/ID is purely combinational, nothing stores it), so after the stall the
same address must be fetched again and fails again with p=0.22. An offline replay in earlier
rounds put the cycle gain of banking those fetches at ~7% (4.4255M -> ~4.11M for a depth-2
queue; r4s2 depth-4 actually hit 4.086M). Three queue attempts (r4s2 -3.05%, r5s2 +0.65%,
r8s0 +1.67%) realised the cycles but lost ~5-6% Fmax, which r8s0 attributed to the queue's own
logic (`qv0 ? Q0 : imem_data` head mux stacked on the flush mux in front of decode/imm_gen/
load-use/ID target adder, plus `stall_id` fanning into queue enables). This attempt keeps the
gain but shrinks the cost to the minimum: one skid entry, and the head mux is folded into the
mux that already exists (`flush ? NOP : imem_data` becomes one LUT4 per bit:
`qv ? Q.instr : (imem_ready ? imem_data : NOP)`). In the timed netlist `imem_data` is a plain
LFSR flop (fpga/core_bench_si.sv), so the instruction-side cone launches at ~0.5 ns, ~1.8 ns
earlier than the dmem BSRAM DO -> load align -> bypass path that is the champion's worst path
(15.26 ns, 8 cells), so one LUT of head mux has slack to land in.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add ONE skid entry {pc, pc_plus4, instr, qv} in if_stage.sv. Fetch address stays `pc` (the
address of the NEXT fetch); BTB lookup, training, `pc+4`, redirect and the EX/MEM.redir late
redirect are unchanged.

Head view (replaces the combinational IF/ID payload; this is what ID decodes):
  head.instr    = qv ? Q.instr    : (imem_ready ? imem_data : 32'h00000013)
  head.pc       = qv ? Q.pc       : pc
  head.pc_plus4 = qv ? Q.pc_plus4 : pc + 4
  head.valid    = qv | imem_ready
Head consumed ("take") = !stall_id (stall_id = dmem_stall | load_use | md_stall, as today).

Next-state (redirect has priority: qv <= 0, pc <= redirect_target):
  adv     = imem_ready & !(qv & stall_id)       // pc <= next_pc (BTB-predicted or pc+4)
  capture = imem_ready & (qv ^ stall_id)        // Q <= {pc, pc+4, imem_data}
            (qv=0 & stalled: bank the head; qv=1 & taken: refill Q with the newly fetched N)
  qv_next = capture | (qv & stall_id)
With qv=1 and the ID stage still stalled both pc and Q hold (depth 1: the extra fetch is
simply redone later). When Q is consumed and imem fails, qv drops to 0 and the core is back in
the zero-latency bypass mode, so the skid adds no latency to the steady state and exactly one
banked fetch is carried across each back-end stall, hiding one later imem failure.

Verify path: ex_stage already compares `fetch_pc = if_id_w.pc` (flop-to-flop 30-bit compares
`eq_tgt`/`eq_ft`/`eq_jalr`); with the skid `if_id_w.pc` is head.pc, which is exactly the
fetch-order successor of the instruction in EX (Q.pc when banked, `pc` otherwise), so the
prediction check stays correct and only gains the 2:1 head.pc mux in front of a flop-to-flop
compare that has slack. The wrong-path population on a redirect is unchanged (EX squash via
EX/MEM.redir, head killed by flush_id, Q cleared by redirect). Under a held dmem stall the
registered `redirect` stays set for several cycles and keeps rewriting `pc` and clearing
`qv`, same as the champion.

hazard_unit.sv: `stall_if` and `flush_if` are no longer consumed by if_stage (pc enable and
NOP injection move into if_stage's adv/head logic); `stall_id`, `flush_id`, `stall_ex_mem`,
`hold_mem_wb` are untouched. `adv` is a function of the same `load_use` cone that `stall_if`
already used for the pc CE, so the pc-enable depth does not grow.

most back-end stall episodes are 1 cycle), Fmax within ~2% of 94.8 MHz, cost ~100 flops and

the fallback is to leave Q untouched and drop only the `head.pc`/`pc_plus4` muxes by storing

an instruction dropped or duplicated across the skid breaks rvfi_order.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-003-r10s2 (regression, -10.14%): A depth-1 fetch skid (one `{pc, pc_plus4, instr, qv}` entry, head mux folded into the existing imem NOP mux, `adv`/`capture` replacing `stall_if` on the pc enable, `in.valid ? ctrl_decoded : '0` added in id_stage) scored 192.41 vs the 214.12 champion, the worst of four fetch-buffer attempts (r4s2 -3.05%, r5s2 +0.65%, r8s0 +1.67%) against a ~+5% cycle estimate, so it would need ~-15% Fmax and queue depth, head-mux LUT count and the verify-compare cone are all ruled out as the lever (r8s0's "retry at depth 1" suggestion is now tested and failed); no worst-path report or cycles/Fmax split was recorded so the cause is inferred, but the "imem_data is an early LFSR flop with ~1.8 ns slack" premise ignored that r9s1 moved the bypass into ID, so the head instr/pc now sit in front of the regfile read -> ID forward-hit compare -> operand flops, load-use and ID target-adder cones, while `stall_id` (load-use | dmem | md_stall) fans into pc/Q/qv enables, so stop trying to buffer fetches in front of ID (cycle win ~5-7% is real but never survives Fmax here) unless a fresh worst-path report shows a cone with slack.

title: Dedicated no-reset shamt flops in ID/EX to cut the fan-out-84 on b_val[4:0], plus a one-LUT late select for ex_result[0]
motivation:
I ran `make timing` on the champion (option 0: 99.98 MHz, worst path 15.297 ns) and read the
per-cell report instead of guessing. The worst path is NOT carry propagation: the 29 ALU
carry cells cost 0.035 ns each (~1.0 ns total), so a carry-select adder (my first idea) would
save <=0.5 ns and is dropped. The 10.0 ns of data path (after the 5.33 ns clock insertion) is:
  tC2Q b_val[0] 0.23 | net b_val[0] (FANOUT 84) -> compare-chain CIN 2.86 (28%!) |
  carry chain 1.0 | net chain-out -> branch_taken LUT 1.23 | 3 LUTs building ex_result[0]
  (branch_taken_s5 -> ex_result_0_s8 -> _s3 -> _s0, 1.3 ns cell + 0.6 net) |
  net ex_result[0] -> ID 1.34 | rs2_fwd LUT + b_d LUT 0.83 (+0.25 net).
Two things stand out. (1) b_val[0] has fan-out 84 because it is shamt[0]: it selects the first
barrel-shifter stage of SLL/SRL/SRA (32 muxes x up to 3 shifters), so the same flop that starts
the 32-bit compare/add chain also drives the shifter, and its net is 2.86 ns. The same applies
to b_val[4:1]. (2) bit 0 of ex_result is the only bit that also receives the SLT/SLTU
carry-out, and it is built by a 3-LUT chain behind the compare carry before the ID bypass.
Paths 2-5 of the report are all within 0.01 ns of path 1 (15.29), so the placer has equalised
many cones; relieving the high-fan-out operand-bit nets helps every cone that starts at an
operand flop, not just this one.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
(a) Add a 5-bit `shamt` field to the ID/EX register (id_ex_t) captured from the same
`b_d[4:0]` value and under the same `!stall` enable as b_val, but WITHOUT the sync reset
(it is only consumed when a valid shift is in EX, always after a capture, so reset-free is
safe; it also makes the flop a different primitive from b_val[4:0] so Gowin synthesis cannot
merge the duplicate back). alu.sv takes `shamt` as a port (from in.shamt) instead of
`shamt = b[4:0]`, so the shifter's 32..96 sinks load the 5 shamt flops and b_val[4:0]
keep only the adder/compare/logic/muldiv-capture sinks (~10-15 sinks). Cost: +5 flops, no
logic, no cycle change. Expected: the 2.86 ns net on the worst path drops to ~1 ns, and the
placer is no longer pulling the ALU chain start toward the shifter's cluster.
(b) In ex_stage/alu, restructure ex_result[0] so the SLT/SLTU carry-out passes through exactly
one LUT before the ID bypass: precompute `bit0_other` (ADD/SUB/logic/shift/LUI/jump/muldiv bit

branch_taken/branch_cond sharing must not sit in front of it). That deletes ~2 of the 3

title: Split EX into an early side path and late adder-class legs: registered one-hot class selects put the carry chains one LUT from ex_result, branch compare moves to rs1_val/rs2_val
motivation:
The champion's worst path (r10s0 log: arrival 15.297 ns / slack -5.0 on a 5 ns constraint, i.e. ~10 ns
achieved, 37 cells, 12 logic levels) is ID/EX reg_q.b_val_0 -> the 32-cell carry chain inside
cpu/u_ex/u_alu (cells alternate u_ex / u_ex/u_alu, so it is the SLT/SLTU/ADD/SUB compare-or-add chain
from bit 0 to bit 31) -> ALU 11-way `case (op)` output mux -> ex_stage result_sel (jump / muldiv
merge) -> id_stage `a_sel_ex ? ex_result : ...` bypass -> ID/EX a_val/b_val flop (it ends on bit 0,
i.e. the SLT/SLTU result bit, which is the only chain output that lands on bit 0). That is the
ALU -> bypass -> ALU loop that r9s1 created by moving the bypass to the operand register. Everything
between the carry-chain output and the capture flop is a LUT level that only exists because the late
adder-class results are muxed *together with* the early ones (logic ops, shifter, LUI, PC+4,
muldiv result) through a decoded 5-bit `op` case: the synthesizer builds an 11-way mux whose select
decode and early legs are all in series with the late legs. Prior single-level trims of this cone
(r3s1 shared adder with `b^sub`, r9s0 result_sel removal, r10s1 flat AND-OR) each either relocated
a late input or added a post-chain XOR, so the lever has not been tried as a clean structural split:
everything that does NOT depend on a carry chain is computed on its own side path from flops, and
the chains meet it at the very last mux with registered one-hot selects.
A second, independent contributor is fan-out: a_val[i]/b_val[i] drive ~10-12 sinks each (ADD, SUB,
SLT, SLTU chains, three bitwise ops, shifter, jalr_sum, and the branch-compare chains: eq, lt, ltu),
while the rs1_val/rs2_val flops, which hold the identical post-forward values for branches, only feed
the store-data / RVFI path. Using rs1_val/rs2_val for the branch compare roughly halves the sink
count on the critical a_val/b_val flops at no cycle cost (alu_src = 0 and auipc = 0 for branches,
so rs?_val == a_val / b_val bit for bit).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the EX datapath (no cycle-count change, no change to bypass/hazard/BTB behaviour) into
two parallel sides that merge at one final AND-OR level:

(1) Registered one-hot result-class selects. decoder/id_stage derive, from the decoded op, four
    late-class flags `l_add`, `l_sub`, `l_slt`, `l_sltu` that are stored in ctrl_t (cleared by the
    existing bubble clears like the rest of ctrl). They are 1 only for ADD-class ops that
    really write the adder result: ADD/ADDI/AUIPC/loads/stores (address = a+b, store/load alu_result
    is the address) and branch-free R/I-type ops; they are 0 for JAL/JALR (PC+4 replaces the sum), for
    MUL/DIV (muldiv result) and for every early op, so the classes are mutually exclusive by
    construction. No decode on the op field remains in the EX result cone.

(2) Early side path (flop-to-flop, finishes while the carry chains are still rippling): in
    ex_stage / alu.sv compute `early_val` = AND-OR of {AND, OR, XOR, SLL, SRL, SRA, LUI} (each gated
    by a registered early-class select, again one-hot, or use the existing alu_op case on this side
    only), merged with the existing jump PC+4 / muldiv-result alternate (`alt_sel ? alt_val : ...`,
    which is already a flop-only function). `early_val` is all-zero whenever a late class is
    selected. The shifter and logic unit keep taking the a_val/b_val flops.

(3) Late adder-class legs, one chain each exactly as inferred today (`a + b`, `a - b`,
    `$signed(a) < $signed(b)`, `a < b`; do NOT share/XOR operands, r3s1 showed that deepens the
    chain): ex_result = early_val | ({32{l_add}} & add_res) | ({32{l_sub}} & sub_res)
    | {31'b0, (l_slt & slt) | (l_sltu & sltu)}. Bits 31:1 see only add/sub/early (<=5 inputs ->
    one LUT4 + MUX2_LUT5 level with `l_sub` as the mux select); bit 0 additionally sees SLT/SLTU.
    The chain outputs therefore sit one LUT level before ex_result instead of ~3 (op decode, 11-way
    case, result_sel), and the id_stage bypass mux is the only level after that.
    Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS the existing algebraic stand-ins stay in alu.sv's ALTOPS arms and the
    old case-based path is used (ifdef), so the formal contract is untouched.

(4) Fan-out split: ex_stage's branch-condition compare (eq / lt / ltu chains) reads
    in.rs1_val / in.rs2_val instead of in.a_val / in.b_val (identical values for branches). jalr_sum

lesson from r3s1/r7s0.

title: Move the redirect-target select out of EX: register taken_eff, mux branch_target/pc_plus4 in MEM
motivation:
Predictor cycle upside is capped (~52k redirects x 2 cycles = ~2.3% of 4.4M cycles;
r9s2 gshare lost 8% to Fmax), so a predictor-slot change can only pay through Fmax at
identical cycles. Fresh make-timing on the champion (place_option 0, 99.98 MHz) shows
the top ~14 setup paths all within 0.05 ns (data delay ~9.95 ns): ALU/compare carry
chain -> ex_result -> ID/EX, imem_ready -> ID/EX, pc -> pc, and
ID/EX.a_val_7 -> EX/MEM.pc_next_1. The last one is the redirect-target data cone:
actual_next = jalr_go ? jalr_target : (exp_ft ? pc_plus4 : tgt) selects between three
already-known 32-bit values with the LATE branch_cond / misalign_fault, so 32 pc_next
flops sit behind the compare carry chain and branch_taken fans out to ~35 sinks. The
value is consumed only when EX/MEM.redir is set (pc <= pc_next in the NEXT cycle) and
by RVFI pc_wdata (untimed), so the select does not need to happen in EX at all.

title: Take the imem NOP mux off the instr bus (valid-gated ctrl) and register ALU result selects so both co-critical cones drop a level
motivation:
The last four rounds localise the remaining Fmax wall to two cone families that sit within
~1 ns of each other, so cutting either one alone is re-bound by the other:
  (a) the EX loop: ID/EX a_val/b_val flop -> plain inferred a+b / a-b / < / <u carry chains ->
      19-way op case -> result_sel -> ex_result -> ID bypass mux -> a_val/b_val/rs?_val flops
      (champion r10s0 worst path: reg_q.b_val_0 -> ... -> reg_q.b_val_0, 37 cells, 15.30 ns);
  (b) the fetch/ID cone: imem_ready (flop) -> flush_if -> `flush ? NOP : imem_data` LUT on every
      instr bit -> rs1/rs2 address -> load-use compare (4 x 5-bit compares) -> stall_if / stall_id
      -> pc enable and the ~260 ID/EX CE pins (r11s1 worst path once (a) was shortened:
      stall_gen/imem_ready -> cpu/u_if -> cpu/u_id -> cpu/u_if/pc, 12 cells, 14.89 ns), and
      instr -> regfile read -> bypass mux -> operand flops, instr -> imm_gen -> tgt adder.
Evidence that (a) alone is not enough: r11s1 (registered one-hot l_add/l_sub/l_slt/l_sltu selects,
untouched inferred chains) lifted Fmax 102.5 -> 106.6 at identical cycles (234.84, +3.96%) but
was rejected by the 4.6% bar because the worst path then moved to (b). Evidence that (b) is
separable from timing noise: it is the one cone where a pure control change (not a datapath
rewrite) removes a LUT level from every launch point (lfsr/imem_data bits AND imem_ready).
In this wrapper imem_data (LFSR flops) and imem_ready (stall_gen flop) are both early flops,
so the NOP mux is a pure extra LUT level in front of the whole ID cone.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Two coordinated cuts, each with a measured or structurally-argued payoff, both pure control
(no hand-written adders/comparators, which lost in r3s1/r7s0/r11s0):

(1) Fetch cone: remove the `flush ? 32'h13 : imem_data` mux from if_stage's out.instr
    (instr = imem_data unconditionally; out.valid = !flush stays). The imem-stall bubble is
    then expressed only by valid=0, and id_stage gates the decoded ctrl: in the `!stall`
    branch of the ID/EX register, `ctrl <= in.valid ? ctrl_decoded : '0` (implemented as the
    flop's sync-reset term: clear ctrl and valid when `flush || (!stall && !in.valid)`), so a
    garbage instruction on an imem-stall cycle can never reach EX/MEM as a live LOAD/STORE
    (mem_stage's dmem_ren/wen are driven from ctrl, not valid) and never forwards
    (reg_write cleared). Safety argument for the hazard side: on an imem-stall cycle stall_if is
    already 1 (imem_stall), a spurious load_use_hazard from garbage rs1/rs2 only adds
    stall_id/flush_id, and flush_id bubbles valid/ctrl exactly like the valid=0 gate does; if
    dmem_stall/md_stall hold ID/EX the garbage is not captured at all. Redirect behaviour is
    unchanged (flush_id still kills the wrong-path instruction). The data fields of an invalid
    slot (rs1_val, tgt, instr...) become garbage rather than NOP-derived, which is already the
    rule for flush_id bubbles (every consumer is valid/ctrl-qualified; BTB training requires
    ctrl.is_branch/is_jump which are zero; RVFI retires only valid). Effect: instr bits are
    raw flop outputs, one LUT level shallower into regfile read / load-use / imm_gen / tgt
    adder, and imem_ready no longer fans out to 32 instr LUTs.
(2) EX loop (the r11s1 recipe, which was correct and scored 234.84 at unchanged cycles):
    decode registered one-hot result selects l_add/l_sub/l_slt/l_sltu into ctrl_t (set in
    decoder.sv; also set for branches only where the compare is shared), keep the carry chains
    as plain inferred `a+b`, `a-b`, `$signed(a)<$signed(b)`, `a<b` operators exactly as today,
    and merge them through an AND-OR keyed by the registered selects together with a small
    early side path (AND/OR/XOR/shifts/LUI, jump pc+4, muldiv result), so no op-code decode or
    11-way case sits behind a carry chain; move the branch-condition compare to the
    rs1_val/rs2_val flops to halve the a_val/b_val sink count. Do NOT rewrite how SLT/SLTU or
    branch compares are expressed (r11s0 -20%) and do not touch the `shamt` fan-out.
    The RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS arm in alu.sv must keep working (select bits for MUL..REMU ALTOPS
    stand-ins stay op-code driven under that ifdef).

Why bundle: r11s1 shows (a) is worth ~+4% and then exposes (b) as the next bound (106.6 MHz);
(b) shortens exactly that bound. Expected ~+8% Fmax at identical cycles (the NOP-mux removal
does not change cycle counts: a load-use false positive during an imem stall is absorbed by
the stall that is already in force).

4,538,902 +/- a few hundred (a cycle change means a stall interaction was altered); then
`make timing TARGET=bench` and read the new worst path before iterating.

title: Late-select fusion: registered one-hot adder legs merged at the ID operand flop, imem_ready off the ID cone
motivation:
The champion (225.90, 102.5 MHz, 4.539M cycles) is bound by a single-cycle loop:
ID/EX a_val/b_val flop -> 32-bit carry chain in alu.sv -> 19-way alu_op case ->
result_sel -> ID bypass 3:1 mux -> a_val/b_val flop (37 cells, 12 levels in the r10s0
report). Same-round r11s1 split EX into an early side path plus plain inferred a+b / a-b /
< / <u legs picked by registered one-hot ctrl_t selects, left the carry chains untouched,
and scored 234.84 (+3.96%, 106.6 MHz, cycles unchanged, formal and cosim passed). It lost
only to the 4.6% bar and the P&R seed spread. Its new worst path was NOT the ALU loop any
more but stall_gen/imem_ready -> if_stage NOP mux (flush ? 0x13 : imem_data) -> ID
(regfile address / load-use compare) -> hazard -> if_stage pc CE (14.894 ns, 9 levels).
So the ALU leg is already relieved and the next bound is a different cone that r11s1 did
not touch. The remaining one-hot merge in EX followed by the ID bypass mux is still two
separate select levels on the adder-result -> operand-flop path. Both cones can be cut
together, and neither adds state or fetch-side logic.
Prior fetch-buffer attempts (r4s2/r5s2/r8s0/r10s2) all failed on Fmax, so this proposal adds
no fetch queue, no predictor state and no new flops on the pc cone. It only deletes mux
levels. Cycles stay identical by construction.

early-flop-only signals off the front of the decode cone".

(A) Fuse the EX result select into the ID operand bypass. Keep r11s1's decomposition. The
decoder emits registered one-hot ctrl_t bits l_add (ALU_ADD and not is_jump, i.e.
ADD/ADDI/AUIPC/load/store address), l_sub, l_slt, l_sltu. Every other op (AND/OR/XOR/SLL/
SRL/SRA/LUI, JAL/JALR link = pc_plus4, MUL/DIV = md_result) goes through one early
`side_res` (registered select inputs only, no carry chain behind it). ex_stage computes
plain inferred `sum = a_val + b_val` (this is the existing `jalr_sum`, shared), `dif =
a_val - b_val`, `lt`, `ltu` (leave `a < b` / `$signed` operators exactly as Gowin infers
them; do NOT hand-share the adder or rewrite the compare, per r3s1/r7s0/r11s0). The
branch compare reads rs1_val/rs2_val so the a_val/b_val sink count drops (as in r11s1).
ex_stage still forms the merged `ex_result` (AND-OR of the legs under the one-hot flops)
for the EX/MEM.alu_result flop. In addition it exports the individual legs (sum, dif, slt
bit, side_res) and the one-hot flags to id_stage. id_stage then builds each operand's
bypass as one flat AND-OR of {sum, dif, side_res, mem_load, early value}, with the
selects computed only from early signals (hit1_ex/hit2_ex over IF/ID bits and ID/EX
flops, ANDed with the registered l_* flags, auipc/alu_src folded in as today). This
removes the separate "alu one-hot merge -> bypass mux" level pair from the adder -> operand
flop path. Bit 0 additionally ORs the slt/sltu bit. Keep the existing jump_misal_ex /
mem_rw_post_trap gating of hit terms unchanged (a trap-killed JAL/JALR must still fall
through to the I-2 source). Keep `sel_ld` exclusive with the EX legs as in the champion.
Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS keep the alu.sv ALTOPS arms (a+b ^ const etc.) reachable on the
side leg so the formal-mode ALU results are unchanged. Real muldiv keeps md_op ->
md_result on side_res.

(B) Take imem_ready off the instruction / regfile / load-use cone. Today `flush_if =
!imem_ready` muxes instr to NOP before rs1/rs2 addresses, decoder, imm_gen and the hazard
compare, adding one LUT input to every one of those cones, and r11s1 showed this is the
next worst path (imem_ready -> NOP mux -> load-use compare -> stall_if -> pc CE). Change
if_stage so out.instr = imem_data unconditionally and out.valid = 1. Move the bubble to the
ID/EX register: hazard_unit `flush_id = (load_use_hazard || redirect || imem_stall) &&
!dmem_stall && !md_stall`. The flush already clears valid + ctrl_t and leaves the data
flops as plain CE flops (r6s0 showed flush fan-out on those ~25 flops is cheap). This is
safe because (1) pc already holds on imem_stall via stall_if, which does not depend on the
instruction; (2) a garbage instruction in ID during an imem stall can only raise a spurious
load_use_hazard, which raises stall_id (hold ID/EX data fields) together with flush_id
(valid/ctrl cleared). That is exactly the existing load-use bubble, and the instruction in
ID/EX is still consumed by EX/MEM this cycle; (3) the bubble's data fields are never
consumed without valid / ctrl qualification, same as every existing bubble; (4) under
dmem_stall / md_stall the ID/EX register still holds whole (flush is masked), as today.
imem_ready then reaches only the pc CE (through stall_if's OR) and the 25 valid+ctrl flush
terms, both a short, flop-launched path. The `flush` input of if_stage becomes unused.

Expected effect: cycles unchanged (4.539M). Fmax: the ALU/bypass loop loses roughly one
more LUT level beyond r11s1 and the imem_ready -> ID cone loses one level, so the median
should rise from ~102.5 to ~109-112 MHz (r11s1 alone reached 106.6 with the imem_ready
cone binding). Area is flat: no new storage beyond the four ctrl_t bits (they ride
through ID/EX and EX/MEM; unused EX/MEM copies are pruned).

title: Look-ahead BTB: pre-read the next fetch's entry into flops so the 64:1 BTB mux leaves the pc->next_pc cone
motivation:
The remaining predictor headroom in cycles is tiny: ~52k EX redirects x 2 bubbles is ~2.3% of the
~4.54M timed cycles even for a perfect predictor (LESSONS r9s2), so every history/RAS/capacity upgrade
(r9s2 gshare -8%, r2s2 JAL/RAS predecode ~0, r3s2/r7s2 already banked) has a ceiling below the 4.6%
acceptance bar and tends to add fetch-cone logic that costs Fmax. The only predictor lever left is
Fmax: the fetch cone is currently pc flops -> 6-bit index -> 64:1 mux of 25 BTB bits (tag[5:0],
ctr[1], tgt[17:0]; ~3 LUT/MUX levels with a high-fanout index) -> 6-bit tag compare -> hit ->
next_pc mux -> pc D/CE. Recent worst paths sit in this region (r11s2: pc_2 -> pc_8, 16 cells; r11s1:
imem_ready -> stall_if -> pc_4, 12 cells) and the champion's EX bypass loop is only ~1-2 ns ahead of
it, so shortening the fetch cone is needed for any Fmax gain from the EX-side work (r11s1's ALU split
scored 106.6 MHz with the fetch/stall cone as its new worst path). The design uses only 5161/10000
LUT4 and 3345 FF, so duplicating mux hardware (resources, not depth - LESSONS r5s1) is affordable.
